title: Priority lane allocator for account escalations with staged fallbacks
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a deterministic 'priority lane allocator' that converts incoming account escalations and top-customer intake signals into an actionable lane assignment and staged fallback policy. Goal: reduce manual Triage for VIP escalations by 70%, standardize decisioning across PM/SE/Eng, and enable automated fallback behaviors that keep customer-facing features live while engineering capacity is constrained. Scope: 1) scoring function (revenue, contract tier, incident severity, recent feature dependency, number of affected users, legal/regulatory flag); 2) lane definitions (Fast-Track, High-Cadence, Standard, Monitor-only); 3) staged fallback policies (region reroute, model-variant fallback, scope-slice, defer to next release); 4) control surface in Console (view assignment, override, audit trail) and API for integrations (Support, CSM, Solutions Eng). Acceptance criteria: - End-to-end evaluation on synthetic dataset with known VIP escalations shows 70% reduction in manual reassignments. - Console view surfaces lane, reason vector, and recommended fallback. - Rollout supports canary to 10% accounts, with automatic rollback if CSAT drop >5 points. Metrics: manual triage count, time-to-assignment, SLA breach rate, CSAT on escalations, # of automated fallbacks executed. Out-of-scope: billing-level contract negotiation and legal approvals (these remain manual). Implementation notes: initial implementation as rules+weights stored in Config Service; next phase will move to ML-scored model if business signals show high variance. Document and template links: Confluence plan: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CP/priority-lane-allocator; Design mocks: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PRIORITY-LANE-MOCKS; Draft API spec: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api-specs/pull/212
comments: 2025-02-17 - Kickoff with SE/Support/CSM. Agreed scoring signals; SE requested 'feature-dep' weight be tunable per product area.

2025-02-21 - Engineering design review. Eng requested smaller MVP: implement deterministic rules engine in Config Service first, postpone ML model. ENG feedback: add per-account override TTL and audit events. Action: ENG to spike rules engine (ENG-4510).

2025-02-28 - PM review with Growth. Proposed lane names changed to Fast-Track / High-Cadence / Standard / Monitor-only to avoid 'VIP' wording. Decision: lane assignment must include human-readable justification (top 3 contributing signals).

2025-03-03 - Security review intake created. SSO/Audit requirement noted for Console overrides. Security flagged KMS access for storing override tokens. Link: https://security.redwood.ai/queue/SECR-2201

2025-03-05 - Prototype demo to Solutions Eng. Demo used synthetic incidents; observed 12% false positives where low-revenue internal partner was flagged due to repeated support pings. Action: add 'internal_partner' negative weight and weekly decay on support-signal.

2025-03-06 - Decision log: Proceed with rules-based MVP gated by canary. Engineering to ship config UI for overrides and audit events in runtime-1.22. PM to author runbook for manual escalation overrides during rollout.
